notes: Well-formed; keys parse to the standard manifest set, and `claude plugin validate --strict .` passes. The `version` key doubles as the minimum tp version session-start.sh compares against - overloaded but deliberate and documented at session-start.sh:6-8. Confirmed the read works: a shimmed `tp --version v0.35.0` passes the gate while the real dev binary (v0.34.3-dev) is refused, exactly as L46-49 says.

Valid JSON; SessionStart and PreToolUse carry matchers and Stop correctly carries none (Stop takes no matcher in Claude Code). The matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit lines up with the two path keys both hooks extract, verified by feeding each tool shape through. The declared timeout of 10 is the bound the Stop hook overruns; that finding is recorded once, on stop-role-incomplete.sh, rather than split across both files.

Round 4's FAIL (symlink-spelling-path-comparison) is repaired; I re-ran the exact failing case rather than reading physical_path. With $PWD=/private/tmp/... and TP_ROUND_DIR=/tmp/..., the unit's own .part file is allowed (exit 0), as are the reverse pairing and the relative spelling. Denials still hold: sibling role, the final .ndjson name, and the no-env fail-closed case - all exit 2, hint naming the one writable file.

Exercised, not read. Denied with exit 2 and a hint naming the owning tp command: .tp/config.json, .TP/config.json, .tp//config.json, .tp/./config.json, .tp/locks/../config.json, /a/b/.tp/local.json, *.tasks.json, .tp-review/*. Allowed with exit 0: README.md, source, the bare .tp-review directory, notes.tasks.json.bak. A path spelled inside file CONTENT does not trip it. Backslash spellings are refused with a reason, i.e. fail closed.

Ran all three paths. Below-minimum tp: exit 2, message plus install hint on stderr, stdout empty. Current tp (shim at v0.35.0): exit 0, 964 bytes of `tp resume --compact` on stdout - bounded, channels clean. Outside a tp cycle: exit 0, silent, session not blocked. Confirmed `tp resume` exits 0 even with the spec-stale blocker, so the `|| exit 0` at L105 does not swallow orientation for a blocked cycle, only for a non-cycle repo.

Predicate is right: ran 11 cases (missing/empty/valid/array-line/trailing-comma/leading-zero/bad-u-escape/truncated/non-role/stop_hook_active/escalation) and every verdict matched a real parser. Falsified is L56-63's 'bounds the time': a 1MB single line takes 4-7s idle but 9.88/10.28/10.30/10.37s with four concurrent siblings, against hooks.json's timeout 10. Past it the runtime kills the hook, exit is not 2, and the runaway it exists to block stops unblocked.

Ran the contract it guards rather than reading it: holding .tp/locks/run-spec.lock from a separate process, `tp run` exits 4 with {error,code:4,hint:'a tp run is already driving spec; ...'} on stderr, and `tp set` mid-hold exits 0. The exit-4 mapping is separately pinned by runner_shape_exit_internal_test.go:64, so no contract gap. The test also pins 2-space pretty JSON.

Round 4's swallow is half-repaired: stderr warns now, the JSON still says clean. Ran both halves on one project whose task file overrides review_max_rounds=3: parseable .tp/config.json -> deviations lists 3 vs 9; truncated config -> exit 0, {project_config:true,deviations:[]}, indistinguishable from clean, --strict also 0, and --quiet removes the stderr notice too. L139-141 already puts `skipped` in the payload for a malformed task file (verified); the config being validated gets no such key.

Ran it: RunLockBusyError maps to exit 4 with an actionable hint naming the cycle, and the refusal is prompt rather than a backoff. RunLockHeld discriminates for real - a hand-written .tp/run-spec.json with stop_reason null gives run_state 'crashed' with no holder and 'in_flight' with one, both observed. No slices reach JSON here. The .gitignore advisory goes through output.Notice, so it is stderr and --quiet-aware.

The one ax-contract-relevant assertion - that the gitignore advisory is an output.Notice and so honours --quiet - is written the right way round: the loud half induces the failure (L167-183) before the quiet half asserts silence, so the quiet assertion cannot pass against a branch that never ran. Hint text and lock path are pinned at L92-94. No JSON-shape surface of its own.

Static plugin manifest: no Go code, no file writes, no locks, no path construction. Nothing in this role's domain. version 0.35.0 matches the release under audit, which is what session-start.sh reads as its minimum.

Static hook manifest: no Go code, no writes, no locks. Commands are ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}-rooted rather than concatenated from input, and each of the three registrations carries the 10s timeout. pre-tool-use-role-write-allow.sh is deliberately absent here; verified it is registered by agents/tp-reviewer.md and agents/tp-auditor.md instead.

RAN IT (9 crafted payloads): allows only role-$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson.part and $TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json; denies the final .ndjson the driver renames to, a sibling role, another unit's escalation, and source. Fails CLOSED (exit 2) with the round env unset. The /tmp vs /private/tmp symlink case resolves and is allowed, so the fence does not over-deny. set -u; file is executable (0755), so the hook is not silently fail-open.

RAN IT (12 crafted payloads): denies .tp/config.json, .tp/locks/../config.json, .TP/config.json, a backslash-escaped spelling, *.tasks.json under notebook_path, an absolute task file and .tp-review/ contents; allows ordinary source, the .tp-review directory itself, a payload whose CONTENT quotes "file_path": ".tp/config.json" (the escaped form cannot match the bare-quote pattern), and a payload with no path. Fails closed on backslash. set -u; executable (0755).

set -u; every substitution guarded with :- ; no writes, no locks, no path built from untrusted input (plugin_root comes from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or $0, manifest via filepath-style concatenation of both). version_part coerces a missing or non-numeric component to 0 before the [ -lt ] test, so a malformed version cannot error the comparison. Errors go through fail() rather than being dropped. Executable (0755).

The comment claims ch()'s block reads removed the 18s/1MB timeout hazard. RAN IT on this machine (awk 20200816, charsplit probe = 1, so blocks ARE engaged): a 1MB single line took 8.6s, 13.6s and 17.5s across three runs and 2MB took 21-22s, past the 10s hooks.json declares. A killed hook reports nothing, so the runaway line this hook exists to block stops the unit unchallenged. The predicate itself is correct: 12 probes all matched §3.3.

Cross-process test. WriteFile uses 0o600, every path via filepath.Join, TempDir resolved through EvalSymlinks. WithRunLock take/release is paired via the acquired/release/held channels with the release in a defer; every runTP exit code is require-checked, no dropped error.

fileExists returns err==nil, so any os.Stat failure reads as absent. RAN IT: temp project, .tp/config.json vs a task file deviating on review_max_rounds; chmod 000 .tp made the command print project_config:false, deviations:[] and exit 0, hiding a real deviation the readable run reports. --strict would pass a gate on an unreadable config. Fix: discriminate with errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist). Rest of the file is read-only and uses filepath.Join throughout.

TryLock is paired with a deferred Unlock (126); no lock-free write path. MkdirAll and TryLock errors are wrapped with %w; the EnsureTPGitignore failure is deliberately non-fatal but reported through output.Notice, not swallowed, and runlock_test pins that channel. Paths built with filepath.Join; RunBase uses filepath.Base so a ../ task-file spelling cannot escape .tp/locks. 0o755 is on the directory, not a file.

Files written 0o600, dirs 0o755, paths via filepath.Join, TempDir EvalSymlinks-resolved. holdRunLock observes a genuine second acquirer rather than taking the lock once; the gitignore-warning test induces the failure (makes .tp/.gitignore a directory) and asserts the loud case before the --quiet case, so the quiet assertion cannot pass against a branch that never ran.

Manifest only: 2-space indent per project convention, version 0.35.0 consistent with the release under audit and read as the preflight minimum by hooks/session-start.sh:86. Nothing in this role's Go-code domain appears in it.

2-space indent, a description naming all three registrations, and every command referenced by ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} exists. The fourth script (pre-tool-use-role-write-allow.sh) is deliberately absent here, not orphaned: agents/tp-reviewer.md:9 and agents/tp-auditor.md:9 register it, with a guard test at internal/cli/plugin_agents_test.go:30.

set -u, every function has a comment stating its rule and why it fails closed on an absent environment, no TODO/FIXME anywhere under hooks/. The physical_path fallback and the symlink rationale record a real regression rather than restating the code; behaviour is covered by internal/cli/role_write_symlink_test.go:84.

set -u, POSIX-only dependencies (awk/grep/sed) consistent with the sibling hooks, and normalize()/denied() are each documented with the spelling attacks they close. The backslash over-denial is named as a deliberate trade with its scope stated, so it is a recorded decision rather than an unmarked shortcut.

set -u, one fail() path so every error carries the same install hint, and the three version helpers are small and separately commented. The comment at 44-49 explicitly corrects an earlier draft of itself about tp's own pre-tag window, which is the convention this repo asks for over a stale claim.

The embedded awk JSON scanner is long but decomposed into one function per grammar production, and the ch() block reader carries the measurement that justifies it (18s on a 1MB line, past the declared 10s timeout) rather than an unexplained optimization. stop_hook_active is honoured so the hook cannot loop; the escalation branch is checked first and separately, as commented.

One cross-process test with a doc comment naming the section it pins; goroutine handoff is fully synchronized (acquired/release/held channels, deferred join), no bare var slice reaches JSON, no TODO. golangci-lint 0 issues over the package.

Re-checked round 4's PARTIAL and it does not survive: workflowDeviations covers all 16 WorkflowOverride fields (model/projectconfig.go 58-83), notify_cmd's absence is documented, and the extract-vs-validate commit_strategy asymmetry is documented at config_extract.go 54-69 with routing to spec/0.35.0-candidates.md section 15. All three JSON slices use make([]T,0); every function under 50 lines.

Every exported symbol carries a doc comment (Error() is the error-interface method, idiomatically exempt); both propagated errors wrap with %w; the gitignore advisory goes through output.Notice rather than raw stderr; no slice reaches JSON. RunLockHeld has a production caller (internal/cli/run_status.go:94), and ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh reports nothing.

Helpers are t.Helper()-marked, release is idempotent, output.Configure is restored via t.Cleanup, and the Notice-channel test induces the failure loudly before asserting the quiet case. Every test name states the rule it pins; no dead helper (deadcode clean).
readCycle goes through the same resume path; tp run --dry-run printed exactly the phase/round/next_units that tp resume --json reported for the same project.

Releasability is checked before caps and maps to StopConverged with exit 0. Engine tests TestRunDriver_StopsConvergedWhenTheOracleReportsRelease and TestRunDriver_ConvergedOutranksACapTheSameIterationReached pass; every non-converged run I drove exited 4.
StopNoUnits is in the vocabulary and ranks last in the precedence table; TestRunDriver_EmptyNextUnitsStopsWithNoUnits passes on the run I executed.
Observed from the fake runner's own timestamps: three role children spawned together, every record/implement child alone.
The fake runner writes no status prose at all, and the loop still advanced implement then audit purely from the task file and the round directory it re-read each iteration.
Caps are evaluated between iterations: with run_max_units=1 the run stopped after one iteration, and a retry inside one iteration overshot by that iteration only, which is what §3.4 allows.
No embedding, vector store or learning-extraction code exists anywhere in the tree; last_failure is a single JSON object holding at most one record, and tp resume is the whole handoff.
The reset is a fresh child process per unit; nothing in the driver or the plugin attempts to clear a caller's context.
tp run --help exposes only --dry-run, --status and the shared flags; there is no cron, interval or schedule surface, and every run I drove ran once and stopped.

Ran tp review --merge on two roles sharing a location: location_clusters appeared while merged_count, duplicates_removed and by_severity were unchanged. No cap stop recorded a round or created .tp-review in any run I drove.
soloIfNotConcurrent truncates any batch containing a non-concurrent kind to one unit; observed at runtime that record, implement and fix units never shared an iteration with anything else.
The driver reads exit codes, the §3.3 predicates on disk, and one spend key from the final log line. A runner whose stdout was pure prose produced no status inference at all.
The eight kinds map onto the existing implement/review/audit/decompose phases and their existing commands; no new task model or review semantics were introduced.

Built and used the seam for the whole audit: it records argv, the full environment, spawn and exit timestamps and the exit code, and takes scripted exits, durable writes, sleeps, spend and escalation from env knobs.
Configured runner.args as ["{nope}"]: tp run exited 2 naming runner.args[0] and listing the five resolvable placeholders, and the fake-runner record directory stayed empty, so nothing was spawned.
With the seam's spend_key each row read 0.25 from the final log line. A runner declaring none reported spend null and printed the unmetered notice at run start; cap-budget never fired for it.
Read .tp/run-spec.json two seconds into a run with 4s children: all three rows carried exit_code, duration_seconds and spend_usd null; after the run the same rows carried 0, 4.01 and 0.
tp run --dry-run printed {next_units, phase, round}, exited 0, spawned nothing (empty fake-runner record dir) and wrote no .tp/run-spec.json.

Observed run_state in_flight mid-run, stopped after a stop_reason, and crashed with the reason nulled and no lock held. On an audit-phase stop the payload carried role_streaks and spec_coverage_clean_rounds; divergence is emitted by the same auditSignalFields tp audit --status uses and is omitted when nil, which is verbatim.
A freshly initialised project's .tp/.gitignore holds local.json, locks/, run-*.json, runs/, rounds/ and last_failure-*.json, covering all four new artifacts.

Ran every numeric field at both endpoints and one step outside (17 calls); all behaved as documented. A task override of 150 beat a project config of 50, which beat the built-in 100. notify_cmd resolved only from .tp/local.json's top-level key.

Ran with TP_FAKE_RUNNER_DURABLE=1,0 so attempt 1 wrote a .part and attempt 2 wrote nothing: the round directory was empty afterwards, proving the leftover .part was deleted before the retry. Each attempt also took a fresh seq and log path.

Every predicate is an existence or content check over named artifacts with no before-state. Disposed an audit row with tp audit --resolve and no source edit whatever, and the oracle stopped returning that audit-fix unit.
All four exited 2 with their hints under TP_UNATTENDED=1 and 0 without it; a cap lowered or set equal exited 0; run_max_budget_usd=0 while 5 resolved exited 2 while 0 where 0 resolved exited 0.

A single run I drove advanced implement (two tasks) then audit (three roles then the record unit). Converged is covered by TestRunDriver_StopsConvergedWhenTheOracleReportsRelease and TestRunDriver_AdvancesThroughImplementAndStopsConverged, both passing.
Set runner.env TP_UNATTENDED=0 in .tp/config.json and had the child print its own value: it printed 1.

An escalating unit stopped the run with the record intact, no last_failure file, and notify_cmd fired. TestRunDriver_ExitTwoWithNoRecordIsAnOrdinaryAttempt and TestRunDriver_InvalidEscalationRecordIsAnOrdinaryAttempt cover the negative cases and pass.

Ran tp escalate with TP_RUN_DIR/TP_UNIT_SEQ set: wrote 5-escalation.json with decision, unit_kind, unit_id, phase, evidence, options[] and at, and exited 2. All five decisions were accepted, a sixth rejected, and with TP_RUN_DIR unset it was a usage error.

Scripted exit 3: the file appeared with the documented fields and a tp-authored summary (command plus log path, no child prose), was surfaced by tp resume and tp brief, survived into the next run, and was cleared by the next success of that same unit.
Ran claude plugin validate in the repo root: validation passed. The plugin ships no binary. Hook payload fixtures are exercised by the hooks tests, and I ran all four hooks by hand against payloads.
All four classes denied with exit 2 and a reason on stderr; a Bash tool_name payload passed with exit 0, so tp's own writes through a shell are outside the matcher.
Ran all three: escalation record present exit 0 even with a malformed .part; neither file exit 2; TP_UNIT_KIND=implement exit 0 without evaluating anything.

With TP_ROUND_DIR set, tp audit emitted /tmp/.../role-spec-coverage.ndjson.part per auditor and tp review emitted role-implementer/tester/architect.ndjson.part per reviewer; with the variable unset no such path appeared. The record brief merges $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-*.ndjson.

Merged two roles reporting §1 under classes x and y: location_clusters carried {location, roles[a,b], severities[blocking], count 2} while merged_count stayed 2 and duplicates_removed 0, so the recorded arithmetic is untouched.

engine.MechanizePhaseQualifier is interpolated into branch 3's directive, and skills/tp/SKILL.md carries the same sentence verbatim at the mechanize-candidate rule and at next_action precedence step 3.

cap-units and cap-budget each produced their own stop_reason in runs I drove, and neither created .tp-review, recorded a round, nor closed a task its unit had not closed. TestRunDriver_ACapStopConcludesNothing passes.

Built a repo with 60 changed files: file_summary reported truncated true, total_changed 60, total_files 50, and the stderr notice named both numbers. Under --quiet the notice was gone but the payload still carried truncated and total_changed.

tp show with 0 and with 2 args each exited 2 with hint 'usage: tp show <id>'; tp reopen with 0 args exited 2; cobra's own completion subcommand with an extra arg exited 2. Commands with no Args validator have no arity to violate.
Both merges report inputs[{path,parsed,skipped}]. review --merge: blank-only 0, zero-byte 0, malformed-only 1, good+malformed 1. audit --merge: blank-only 0, malformed-only 1.
A run with one retried unit reported totals.units 7 in .tp/run-spec.json and units_done 7 in tp run --status, over six distinct units; run_max_units=1 stopped a run after a single attempt.

stopPrecedence lists §3.4's nine in exactly the documented order and highestPrecedence takes all candidates at once rather than testing them in sequence. TestStopPrecedence_RanksTheWholeVocabularyInSection34sOrder and the four ConvergedOutranks/UnitFailureOutranks tests pass.
Observed all three: in_flight while a run held the lock, stopped once stop_reason was set, and crashed after nulling stop_reason in the state file with no lock held.

TP_ROUND_DIR is keyed by cycle (.tp/rounds/<base>/<phase>-r<n>), not by run, so files survive a driver death; a second run over the same round found the collected role files and the record brief's merge guard skips when merged.ndjson exists.

Read the child's own environment from the seam's records: TP_RUN_ID a 26-char ULID, TP_RUN_DIR absolute, TP_ROUND_DIR /abs/.tp/rounds/spec/audit-r1, TP_FILE the resolved task file, plus TP_UNIT_ID/KIND/SEQ, TP_PHASE and TP_ROUND only in the audit phase.

next_units carries {kind,id,brief_command} plus round, and a non-concurrent kind is never returned alongside another (verified at runtime). But §4.1 says next_action's command, brief_command and payload render next_units[0], and only payload does: for an audit-record unit next_action.brief_command was 'tp audit spec.md' vs the unit's merge-then-record brief, and for an audit-fix unit both command and brief_command were 'tp audit spec.md' vs 'tp audit spec.md --status'.
With a role unit that had written neither its .part nor an escalation record, stop_hook_active false exited 2 and stop_hook_active true exited 0 on the identical payload.
A cap stop never touches convergence state: after the cap-units run no review state existed at all. TestRunDriver_ACapStopConcludesNothing asserts the blocking-finding case.

Ran the discriminating experiment my prior round asked for: with project config resolving run_max_units to 200, a task-override set to 150 was ACCEPTED under TP_UNATTENDED (a comparison against the built-in 100 would have refused it), and 300 was refused naming 'the resolved 150'. A project-layer raise to 400 was refused too. TP_RUN_MAX_UNITS=9999 changed nothing. runner and notify_cmd were refused at task, project and local layers.

SIGINT one second into a run with three 3s children: exit 4, stop_reason interrupted, all three children recorded a full 3.00s lifetime and no further unit was spawned. TestRunDriver_SignalStopsTheRunWithInterrupted covers SIGTERM.

A notify_cmd exiting 7 fired on an escalation stop with TP_STOP_REASON=escalation, TP_RUN_ID and TP_ESCALATION_PATH in its environment; the run still reported stop_reason escalation and surfaced the notify exit_code 7 without changing anything.

hooks.json declares timeout 10 on SessionStart, PreToolUse and Stop; agents/tp-reviewer.md and agents/tp-auditor.md declare timeout 10 on the fourth (role-write-allow). Every hook I ran returned in well under a second with an explicit exit code.

Put a fake claude on PATH and read the argv it received: implement got --agent tp-implementer, audit-role got --agent tp-auditor, both after --permission-mode auto. agentByKind lists only the three kinds, so record/resolve/decompose/fix get none.

Wrote one valid role file into the round dir and tp resume returned only the other two roles; replacing one with a malformed file put that role back in the list. The driver's clearUnitArtifacts deletes each returned role's file and .part before spawning, which I confirmed by an empty round dir after a retry.
Read an implement child's whole environment from the seam record: TP_ROUND and TP_ROUND_DIR were absent entirely, not present-and-empty, while every other TP_ variable was there.
Scripted the fake to write a valid record AND perform its durable write AND exit 0: the run still stopped with stop_reason escalation. TestRunDriver_EscalatesWhateverTheHarnessExitedWith passes.
A role file holding one valid object plus the line 'not json' was returned as still-pending by tp resume and was blocked by the Stop hook, so both readers of the predicate reject it.

A file of only blank and whitespace lines merged with exit 0; a file whose sole content line was malformed exited 1 with a hint about trailing commas and wrapping arrays. Same on both review and audit.

From the seam's own timestamps with SLEEP_MS=1500: three audit-role children all spawned at 23:27:18.823 and all exited at 23:27:20.32x, while the two audit-record attempts ran at 20.447-21.949 and 21.967-23.469 with no overlap.
tp off PATH: exit 2 with brew and go install lines. A fake tp reporting v0.30.0: exit 2 naming the plugin's minimum 0.35.0. A fake reporting v0.35.0: exit 0 with tp resume --compact on stdout.
Observed both halves in one run: two roles exited 0 with no durable write and one exited 1 having written its .part, and all three were retried as failed attempts.

Put the same malformed role file in front of all three: tp resume returned the role as pending, the Stop hook exited 2 naming 'a line that is not a JSON object', and the driver treated the attempt as failed and re-ran it.

Ran tp audit --resolve with a role:item_id selector and with a 0-based index, --resolve-all, and --force: same dispositions (fixed/wontfix/duplicate) and flags as the review side. A disposition written with no code change satisfied the audit-fix predicate.

Observed exit 4 for cap-units, cap-budget, escalation, unit-failure, interrupted and driver-error. Exit 0 on converged is pinned by TestRunDriver_StopsConvergedWhenTheOracleReportsRelease and the run_exit_codes tests, all passing.

Ran the allowlist the two role agents register: the unit's own .part and its escalation record were allowed (absolute and relative spellings), while another role's .part, the final .ndjson name, merged.ndjson, a source file and a payload with the naming env unset were all denied.

A map {implement: claude, default: opencode} dispatched implement to claude and the rest to opencode (confirmed by the unmetered notice naming the seven default kinds). A map without default exited 2; an object without cmd was read as a map and exited 2 on its non-kind key.

Ran the record brief's guard against a merged.ndjson holding a wontfix row: the merge was skipped and the disposition survived. Re-recording with TP_ROUND set rewrote that round's entry (review_rounds stayed [1,2]; audit_rounds stayed [1]). A fixed row made tp review --record exit 1 with the re-review hint while tp audit --record counted it as one open finding.

--dry-run exited 0 and wrote no .tp/run-spec.json; --status exited 3 with 'no run state for spec.tasks.json' before any run and 0 afterwards; both ran successfully while another tp run held the lock, so neither takes it.
A role file of one object plus a trailing newline satisfied the predicate, and a file of only blank and whitespace lines satisfied it too, both at the oracle and in the Stop hook.
Restarted tp run over a project whose previous run had stopped and it picked up the same pending unit from disk. TestRunDriver_CrashedDriverResumesAtTheSameUnit passes.

A template of ["x"] had its child's stdout and stderr both land in $TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl. A template of ["{log_path}"] received that same path, wrote it itself, and the driver added no redirect (the child's own stdout never reached the log or the driver's streams).

With a gate scripted to print GATE-BOOM and exit 1: tp done without TP_UNIT_KIND wrote no last_failure file at all, and with TP_UNIT_KIND=implement it wrote one whose summary was 'gate: <cmd>; output: GATE-BOOM'.
Used a runner that reads stdin with head -c 1: it logged STDIN-EOF-OK on every invocation and the run finished well inside a 20s timeout, so stdin is closed rather than left open.

capStop is consulted between iterations only. The SIGINT run demonstrates the same no-kill behaviour directly: three 3s children all completed after the stop condition was raised. TestRunDriver_ACapTrippingMidIterationKillsNothing passes.
Ran tp import --force under six settings: unset, empty and '0' all exited 0; '1', 'false', 'no' and 'yes' all exited 2. Activation is presence and non-emptiness and not-'0', exactly as documented.

The rename to the final name happens only on exit 0. A unit that wrote its .part and exited 1 left only the .part, the oracle counted the role as pending, and the driver deleted that .part before the retry (round dir empty afterwards).

An unmetered runner printed one stderr line at run start: 'spend is not metered: the runner declares no spend_key...'. A map {implement: claude, default: opencode} instead printed 'spend is not metered for review-role, review-record, review-resolve, decompose, audit-role, audit-record, audit-fix'.
With role-implementer.ndjson.part holding one JSON object (and again holding only blank lines) the hook exited 0 and printed nothing.

Compared tp run --status against tp run --status --compact on the same stopped run: compact kept stop_reason, caps, spend_usd, units_done and wall_clock_seconds and dropped the last_unit object with its log path.

tp config --resolved listed all seven with sources; --extract hoisted the six project-level ones into .tp/config.json (notify_cmd correctly excluded as local-only); validate --project reported a runner deviation between the task override and the project config.
TestRunDriver_EmptyNextUnitsStopsWithNoUnits passes; the loop reads next_units once per iteration and does not re-poll.

Pointed the runner at a nonexistent executable: stop_reason driver-error, exit 4, and the single unit row kept exit_code null rather than being charged a failed attempt. TestRunDriver_ARunDirectoryItCannotWriteIsADriverError covers the other half.
Observed in a live run: audit-record was attempted twice (seq 6 attempt 1, seq 7 attempt 2) with run_max_unit_retries at its default 1, then the run stopped with unit-failure.
With a run in flight, tp set <id> estimate_minutes=7 succeeded while a second tp run exited 4 with 'another tp run holds .tp/locks/run-spec.lock'.

No memory layer exists: searched the tree for embedding/vector/pgvector/learning-extraction surface and found none. The handoff is tp resume plus a single last_failure object, which I saw written, surfaced by tp resume and tp brief, and cleared on the next success of the same unit.

Ran a driver run scripting exit 3: .tp/last_failure-spec.json was written with unit_kind/unit_id/phase/exit_code/summary/at, survived into the next run, and tp resume --json plus tp brief both carried it, so a failed verification reaches the next unit.

The loop exits on the oracle's phase, never on a completion string. Confirmed by running the fake runner: its stdout prose was ignored entirely and the phase advanced only when the durable write appeared on disk.

Only converged comes from the oracle; the three caps are separate stop reasons. Ran run_max_units=1 and run_max_budget_usd=1 and got cap-units and cap-budget with no round recorded and no .tp-review created.

Ran all four user-only operations under TP_UNATTENDED=1 and each exited 2 with a hint; ran hooks/pre-tool-use-write-deny.sh over the four fenced paths and each was denied with exit 2; hooks/hooks.json declares timeout 10 on all three plugin hooks and the agent definitions declare it on the fourth.

Ran a runner echoing to both streams: the output landed in $TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl and not in the driver's own output. A runner that reads stdin got EOF immediately rather than hanging. run_max_unit_budget_usd=2 appended --max-budget-usd 2 to the claude argv.

Ran with TP_FAKE_RUNNER_SLEEP_MS=1500: three audit-role children shared one spawn timestamp and overlapped for the full 1.5s, while the two audit-record attempts ran strictly after them and never overlapped each other.
Set runner.cmd to a shell script in .tp/config.json and the driver spawned exactly that executable; an object without cmd is rejected as a per-kind map with a non-kind key, exit 2.

Ran templates using {log_path}, {unit_id}, {unit_kind}, {max_budget_usd} and {prompt}; each expanded to the unit's value in the observed argv. An unknown brace token exited 2 before any child spawned.
Set runner.env to {TP_UNATTENDED:0, FOO:bar}: the child's environment showed FOO=bar merged in and TP_UNATTENDED=1, so env merges over the parent and the driver's own variables are applied after it.

With the seam's spend_key total_cost_usd and TP_FAKE_RUNNER_SPEND=0.25 every run row reported spend_usd 0.25 and totals reached 1.75 over seven attempts. A runner declaring none printed the unmetered notice and reported spend null.
implement units ran one per iteration and were judged complete only once the task's status was done in the task file; two independent ready tasks were never returned together.

Role units wrote role-<id>.ndjson.part; the driver renamed to the final name on exit 0 (observed in .tp/rounds/spec/audit-r1) and the three siblings ran concurrently. A file with an unparseable line failed the predicate and was re-run.

The record predicate is merged.ndjson plus the round file. My run's audit-record unit exited 0 with neither present and was correctly judged a failed attempt twice, and it never overlapped the role units.
allRowsDisposed reads merged.ndjson; at the oracle level a review-resolve unit is returned while any finding lacks a disposition and disappears once all carry one.
taskFileHasTasks is the decompose predicate; it is a plain existence check over the task file and needs no baseline.
Ran three audit-role siblings concurrently against a real corpus; each wrote its own role file, all three were renamed on exit 0, and a malformed one was re-run rather than skipped.

Observed in a live run: audit-record ran alone after the roles, and its predicate (merged.ndjson plus the audit round file) was correctly unsatisfied because the fake runner never ran the record brief.

Ran tp audit --resolve on merged.ndjson with a role:item_id selector and no code change at all; the row gained a resolved object and the oracle stopped returning the audit-fix unit and advanced to the next round.
converged is produced only by the oracle reporting release and is the sole exit-0 reason; it leads the precedence table.
Ran with run_max_units=1: stop_reason cap-units, exit 4, totals.units 1. A retried unit counted again in totals.units (7 attempts for 6 units in another run).
cap-wall-clock is in the vocabulary and TestRunDriver_CapWallClockStopsTheRun passes in the run I executed; I did not wait out a 60s cap by hand.
Ran with run_max_budget_usd=1 and TP_FAKE_RUNNER_SPEND=2: stop_reason cap-budget, exit 4. With the default 0 the cap never fired across a 7-attempt run accruing 1.75.
Scripted the fake runner to write a valid escalation record while exiting 0: the run stopped with stop_reason escalation, exit 4, the record intact and no last_failure.
Observed a unit exhausting 1+run_max_unit_retries=2 attempts (audit-record seq 6 and 7, both exit 0 with no durable write) and the run stopping with unit-failure.

no-units is defined for a non-releasable cycle with no pending unit and ranks last in the precedence table; TestRunDriver_EmptyNextUnitsStopsWithNoUnits and TestRunDriver_ACapOutranksAnEmptyNextUnits pass.
Sent SIGINT one second into a run with three 3s children: stop_reason interrupted, exit 4, all three children ran their full 3s (not killed) and no fourth unit was spawned.
Pointed TP_RUNNER_SEAM at a nonexistent path: stop_reason driver-error, exit 4, error naming the fork/exec failure and a hint about workflow.runner and .tp writability.

TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp done <id> <reason> --skip-gate exited 2 with 'is a user-approved decision and is refused under TP_UNATTENDED' and a tp escalate --decision skip-gate hint; without the variable the same call exited 0.

With review_max_rounds resolving to 3, TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp set --workflow review_max_rounds=9 exited 2 naming the resolved 3 and hinting raise-review-cap; audit_max_rounds behaved the same; both succeeded without the variable.
TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp import <file> --force exited 2 with the import-force escalation hint; the same command exited 0 with the variable unset.
Raising run_max_units above the resolved value exited 2; lowering and equal both exited 0; setting run_max_budget_usd to 0 while 5 resolved exited 2 while 0 where 0 already resolved exited 0.

Ran the hook with tp off PATH (exit 2, install commands), with a fake tp reporting v0.30.0 (exit 2, names the 0.35.0 minimum), and with a fake reporting v0.35.0 (exit 0, emitted tp resume --compact). hooks.json registers it on matcher '*'.

Piped Write payloads through the hook: .tp-review/state.json, spec.tasks.json, .tp/config.json and .tp/local.json each exited 2; internal/cli/run.go and a Bash tool_name exited 0. hooks.json matcher is Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit.

Ran the hook across all cases: non-role kind exit 0; role with no .part and no record exit 2; valid .part exit 0; malformed .part exit 2; malformed .part plus escalation record exit 0; stop_hook_active true exit 0.
tp config --resolved reported run_max_units default 100. tp set --workflow accepted 1 and 10000 and rejected 0 and 10001.
Default 28800 reported by tp config --resolved; 60 and 604800 accepted, 59 and 604801 rejected.
Default 0 reported; 0 and 10000 accepted, 10001 and -1 rejected. The 0 value is inert rather than a zero cap: a run accruing 1.75 never stopped on cap-budget.
Default 0 reported; 0 and 1000 accepted, 1001 rejected. At 0 the claude template omitted the flag pair entirely; at 2 it appended --max-budget-usd 2, observed in a real spawn.
Default 1 reported; 0 and 5 accepted, 6 rejected. With the default I observed exactly two attempts per unit before unit-failure.

tp config --resolved reports runner default 'claude'. All three shapes resolve from .tp/config.json and a task override: a name, an object with cmd, and a per-kind map. tp set --workflow runner= is not a supported route (unknown field), which §7 does not require; extract and validate --project do cover it.

Default unset (empty). Placing notify_cmd in the project workflow block and in the task override both left it at the default; only a top-level notify_cmd in .tp/local.json resolved, with source 'local'.

wrapArityErrors walks the whole command tree after cobra's lazily registered built-ins are on it; tp show with 0 and 2 args, tp reopen with 0, and cobra's completion subcommand with an extra arg all exited 2. tp show's hint is 'usage: tp show <id>'.

--resolve accepted both a 0-based index and a role:item_id selector, --resolve-all disposed the rest, and --force was required to re-resolve. A disposition written with zero code change satisfied the audit-fix predicate and advanced the oracle.

With 60 changed files: file_summary reported total_files 50, truncated true, total_changed 60, and the stderr notice named 60 and 50. Under --quiet the notice vanished and the payload still carried both.

All eight brief commands match §3.3.1 verbatim, including the record kinds' '[ -f merged ] || tp <phase> --merge ...; tp <phase> <spec> --record merged' guard. Succeeded requires exit 0 AND the durable write; I observed both single-condition cases counted as failed attempts.

SIGINT during a run left all three in-flight children to finish their full 3s and spawned nothing more; the run state was written before exit 4. Caps are consulted between iterations only, so nothing is killed.

Read the child's own environment: TP_RUN_ID a 26-char ULID, TP_RUN_DIR absolute, TP_ROUND_DIR .tp/rounds/spec/audit-r1, TP_FILE, TP_UNIT_ID/KIND/SEQ and TP_PHASE. TP_ROUND/TP_ROUND_DIR absent in the implement phase, and runner.env TP_UNATTENDED=0 did not survive the driver's later merge.

README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md all carry tp run, the runner configuration, TP_UNATTENDED and tp escalate, and the plugin's installation and hook behaviour (REFERENCE.md carries the detail). CLAUDE.md's reset-native section now opens with tp run as primary and names subagent-per-unit the interactive fallback.
An unexecutable runner produced stop_reason driver-error and exit 4 with the unit's row left at exit_code null rather than charged a failed attempt.

Drove real runs: state read through the resume path, next_units taken, role kinds spawned together and every other kind alone, state re-read from disk, caps checked. The loop advanced implement then audit; converged and crash resumption are covered by passing engine tests.

A valid record stopped the run with escalation even though the child exited 0 and completed its durable write; no last_failure was written and the artifacts were left in place. The invalid-record and exit-2-with-no-record arms are covered by two passing engine tests.
A fresh tp init wrote .tp/.gitignore holding local.json, locks/, run-*.json, runs/, rounds/ and last_failure-*.json — the four new entries plus the two pre-existing ones.

Preflights tp's presence and compares tp --version against plugin.json's 0.35.0, failing with the brew and go install lines in both the absent and the too-old case; on success it emits tp resume --compact on every matcher (hooks.json uses '*').

Fires only when TP_UNIT_KIND ends in -role; applies the role predicate to the .part and checks $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json. Blocked with neither, allowed with either, exited 0 for implement, and allowed once stop_hook_active was true — all six cases run by hand.

All three plugin hooks declare timeout 10 in hooks.json and the fourth (role-write-allow) declares it in both agent definitions. Every hook I executed returned an explicit exit code immediately rather than blocking.

Matcher is Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit. Denied .tp-review/ contents, *.tasks.json, .tp/config.json and .tp/local.json with exit 2; allowed an ordinary source path and a Bash payload, so tp's own writes through a shell pass.

Ran a failing gate twice on the same project: without TP_UNIT_KIND no file was written; with it, one was, summary 'gate: <cmd>; output: GATE-BOOM'. The shipped tp done behaviour outside a run is unchanged.

.tp/last_failure-spec.json carried unit_kind, unit_id, phase, exit_code, summary and at, with a tp-authored summary naming the command and log path. tp resume and tp brief both surfaced it, it survived into the next run, and the next success of the same (kind,id) cleared it.

tp review --merge emitted location_clusters [{location, roles[], severities[], count}] for a location two roles reported under different classes, and merged_count, duplicates_removed and by_severity were identical to the single-role run.

ReviewNextAction branch 3 interpolates MechanizePhaseQualifier beside the class name, and skills/tp/SKILL.md carries the identical sentence at the mechanize-candidate rule and at next_action precedence step 3.

Both merges report inputs with per-file parsed and skipped counts. An input with content lines none of which parsed exits 1; zero-byte and blank-only inputs exit 0; blank lines are neither parsed nor skipped.

next_units carries {kind,id,brief_command} plus round and a non-concurrent kind is never returned alongside another, all verified at runtime. The acceptance's second clause, 'next_action renders next_units[0]', is only half met: payload.unit names the unit, but command and brief_command keep phase-level forms that differ from the unit's own brief for the record, resolve and fix kinds.

Fired on an escalation stop with TP_STOP_REASON, TP_RUN_ID and TP_ESCALATION_PATH set; exec'd without a shell and split on whitespace; its exit 7 was reported in the run payload and stop_reason stayed escalation.

agents/ declares tp-implementer, tp-reviewer and tp-auditor; the two role agents register a PreToolUse allowlist I ran and confirmed permits only the unit's own .part and its escalation record. The claude template appended --agent tp-implementer and --agent tp-auditor in real spawns and none for the other kinds.

plugin.json declares name, version 0.35.0, description, author, homepage, repository, license and keywords alongside skills/tp, hooks/ and agents/. claude plugin validate passed and no binary is shipped.

Verified at the oracle: with a non-empty panel whose three role files all satisfied the predicate and no recorded round, next_units returned exactly one audit-record unit for round 1. recordUnit is guarded by the round file's presence and by the caller's non-empty-panel check, so an unresolvable panel returns none.

Observed 1+run_max_unit_retries attempts with distinct seq values and distinct log paths. With DURABLE=1,0 the attempt-1 .part was deleted before attempt 2, leaving an empty round directory, so the leftover could not satisfy the retry's predicate.

With TP_ROUND_DIR set, tp review and tp audit each named $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-<that role>.ndjson.part in that role's own prompt; unset, no such path appeared. The record brief merges role-*.ndjson into merged.ndjson only when absent, which preserved a wontfix disposition in my test.

Verified at the oracle: a satisfied role file was omitted, a malformed one put the role back, all three satisfied returned exactly one record unit, and after recording the oracle returned one audit-fix unit at a time keyed role:item_id until it was disposed.
--compact kept stop_reason and the cap totals and stripped last_unit (the per-unit row and its log path), verified by diffing the two outputs on one stopped run.
tp run --dry-run listed the units, exited 0, wrote no run state, spawned nothing, and succeeded while another tp run held the lock.
Observed exit 4 on six different stop reasons and exit 2 on a usage error before the loop started (an unresolvable placeholder, with no child spawned). Exit 0 on converged is pinned by passing tests.

Second tp run over the same task file exited 4 naming .tp/locks/run-spec.lock, while a child-style tp set write succeeded during the same run, so the task-file write lock is never held across a spawn.

.tp/run-spec.json held run_id, started_at, phase, stop_reason, totals and one row per attempt with seq/kind/id/attempt/exit_code/duration_seconds/spend_usd/log_path. Mid-run the rows carried null exit_code and were updated in place afterwards; totals started at zero on each new run.

--status printed phase, units_done, spend against all three caps, last_unit with exit code and log path, stop_reason, and run_state as in_flight/crashed/stopped (I produced all three). It carried the divergence signals on an audit-phase stop, exited 0 when it could report and 3 when no state existed, and worked while a run held the lock.

With .tp/config.json naming runner 'claude' and a fake claude on PATH, setting TP_RUNNER_SEAM spawned the seam instead and claude was never invoked. Its argv was the positional list [kind, id, log_path, max_budget] and spend was read under total_cost_usd.
Ran all three shapes from .tp/config.json. An object carrying cmd resolved as a runner; one without cmd was read as a per-kind map and exited 2; a map without default exited 2.

Spend read from the final log line (0.25 per unit, 1.75 total over 7 attempts) and cap-budget fired at run_max_budget_usd=1 with spend 2. A runner with no spend_key reported null, printed the notice once at run start, and left cap-budget inert; a per-kind map named its unmetered kinds.

Observed the real claude argv: -p <prompt> --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode auto --agent tp-auditor, with no budget flag at 0 and --max-budget-usd 2 at 2. opencode resolved to 'run <prompt>'. An unresolved placeholder exited 2 with nothing spawned.

stopPrecedence is converged, driver-error, escalation, unit-failure, interrupted, cap-budget, cap-wall-clock, cap-units, no-units — §3.4's order exactly — and highestPrecedence resolves by rank rather than by test order.

Produced six of the nine by hand (cap-units, cap-budget, escalation, unit-failure, interrupted, driver-error) and the other three are pinned by passing tests. No stop recorded a round or created .tp-review, and the three attempt counters agreed at 7.

Wrote $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json with all seven documented fields and exited 2; all five decision values accepted and a sixth rejected with the list; TP_RUN_DIR unset was a usage error. Concurrent siblings keeping their own record is covered by a passing engine test.

All four operations exit 2 under the variable and 0 without it; equal or lower caps accepted; a budget field set to 0 while non-zero resolves refused. runner and notify_cmd refused at task, project and local layers. Activation confirmed on unset/empty/0 (inactive) vs 1/false/no/yes (active). No TP_<FIELD> env layer exists to fence.

Eight kinds in table order with each kind's predicate and concurrency. Every predicate reads named artifacts as they are, with no baseline; the role predicate ignores blank and whitespace-only lines, verified on a blank-only file and on one ending in a newline.
A template omitting {log_path} had both streams redirected to $TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl; one using it owned the file with no redirect. Every child saw stdin at EOF rather than hanging.

All seven fields present with documented defaults; 17 boundary calls confirmed both endpoints accepted and one step outside rejected for each numeric field; notify_cmd resolved only from .tp/local.json; --resolved, --extract and validate --project all cover them.
